subject: Hosted API capacity uplift and rate funnel proposal
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Elena Cruz <elena@catalystai.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API capacity uplift and rate funnel proposal

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for taking the time this week — really appreciate the walk-through of your peak patterns. Per our conversation, I pulled together a short set of structured options to get Catalyst out of the throttling window and reduce per-token variability while keeping monthly spend predictable.

Attached: Catalyst-usage-q1.csv (raw tokens by route), draft-uplift-SOW.pdf (terms sketch).

High level options (summary):
- Baseline: keep current hosted plan, add 20% burst pocket (no commit change) — minimal ops work, modest cost headroom.
- Mid-tier (recommended): increase hosted monthly commit to 2M tokens, apply blended rateband for generation/embedding, include a 10% burst credit and soft-throttle guardrails.
- High-tier: commit 5M tokens, lower unit rates, dedicated burst reserve and canary routing to an augmented instance pool.

What I need from you to firm numbers: preferred tier, any strict legal language on data retention, and procurement contact for DocuSign/PO. If you want, I can put the mid-tier into a one-page offer and route to DocuSign today.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm mid/high/baseline preference by EOD Mon 4/5.
2) We provide formal offer and ops appendix (48 hours).
3) Legal/proc executes DocuSign, we schedule a short runbook handoff with Karthik for the rollout.

CCing our billing lead if there are specific invoice cadence requests.

Best,

Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0199

Attachment stubs: draft-uplift-SOW.pdf (PDF, 4 pages), Catalyst-usage-q1.csv (CSV)

From: Elena Cruz <elena@catalystai.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Sloan <michael.sloan@catalystai.com>, Catalyst AI Procurement <procurement@catalystai.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity uplift and rate funnel proposal

Lauren — thanks for the clear options. A few notes from our side after reviewing the usage export:

- Our Q1 average was ~1.1M generation tokens/month but we see spikes (campaigns) that push short-term demand to ~3.2M/day for 2–3 hours. The attached workbook breaks down by route.
- Procurement wants: mid-tier pricing, explicit burst rules, and a simple clause for overage handling (prefer invoice vs auto-charge).
- Legal: we have a standing ask of 90 days data retention for logs (can be negotiated but prefer 90). Any longer is non-starter for regulators.

Can you send a concrete mid-tier offer and the ops appendix so we can review with Michael and get a PO ready? Also please include estimated latency at p95 for the proposed mid-tier commit.

Thanks,
Elena
VP, Product 
Elena Cruz | Catalyst AI
elena@catalystai.com

Attachment: Catalyst-consumption-breakdown.xlsx

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Elena Cruz <elena@catalystai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity uplift and rate funnel proposal

Elena — great detail, thank you. Quoting your note below and responding inline.

On Thu, Apr 1, 2027 at 11:05 AM Elena Cruz <elena@catalystai.com> wrote:
> Our Q1 average was ~1.1M generation tokens/month but we see spikes ...

Summary and concrete mid-tier offer (attached: Catalyst-Redwood-MidTier-Offer.pdf):
- Commit: 2,000,000 tokens/month (12-month term).
- Pricing: blended generation rate $0.00045/token; embeddings $0.00020/token.
- Burst: 10% monthly burst pocket (200k tokens) with manual approval for additional bursts; overage invoiced monthly at 1.25x the blended rateband (no auto-charge without PO).
- P95 latency: projected ~320ms across our hosted pool at current region (us-west) for sequences up to 1k tokens; can push down to ~260ms with prioritized routing at a modest premium.
- Ops/Runbook: we include a two-hour production handoff + a 5-step rollback playbook. Karthik — ops details attached.

Data retention: you noted 90 days. We can accept 90 days as the default for standard logs; longer-term audit logs can be provided under a separate SLA (we'll note the clause in the SOW).

If this aligns, we will:
- Update DocuSign with the mid-tier SOW and the retention language (90 days).
- Send a one-page invoice schedule for procurement and include a PO template.

Kimberly — can you confirm billing cadence options (monthly invoice vs net-30) and whether you need a vendor W9 on file?

Thanks — attaching the formal mid-tier offer and the ops appendix.

Best,
Lauren

Attachments: Catalyst-Redwood-MidTier-Offer.pdf (PDF), throughput-plan-ops.docx (DOCX)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Elena Cruz <elena@catalystai.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity uplift and rate funnel proposal — ops appendix

Elena / Lauren — quick ops confirmation from my side:

- Autoscale & burst behavior: mid-tier commit will keep a warm pool sized for steady-state plus a continuous batching headroom to absorb 2–3 hour spikes up to ~3.5M/day if burst approval is granted. The 10% burst pocket is designed for shorter bursts; for the multi-hour campaign pattern we recommend pre-approved burst requests (we can automate approval for repeat campaigns).
- Soft-throttle: we will enforce a soft-throttle at 95% of commit baseline; soft-throttle notifies and routes to lower-cost model variant instead of hard reject.
- Cache strategy: prefix KV caching on routes with high repetition; this will lower actual token consumption for prompt-heavy campaigns by 8–15% based on the sample export.
- Runbook & handoff: two-hour session, include playbook pages 1–3 for rollback.

Attachment: throughput-plan-ops.docx (internal ops appendix).

Happy to join your procurement call to walk through the approval process.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Serving Operations | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity uplift and rate funnel proposal

Thanks Lauren — the mid-tier looks reasonable and is likely what we'll sign. A couple quick items before legal signs off:

1) Please add explicit language in the SOW that overage invoicing requires an approved PO (we will not accept automatic card/billing charges for post-commit overages).
2) Confirm that the 90-day logs retention will be included and that any longer-retention logs are a separate SLA with explicit opt-in.

Michael (cc'd) is our procurement lead — Michael, can you pick up DocuSign and loop legal? I can provision a PO once DocuSign matches the above.

Please send the updated DocuSign link and a one-page invoice schedule; we will triage next week.

Many thanks,
Elena Cruz
VP, Product | Catalyst AI
